speechtext: Whose report is that?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
That is the report of Miss Hyndman, K.C. That is what Mrs. West told them when they were here in Ottawa. Further on she says:
To use Mrs. West's words it "overstimulates the will of the volunteer to serve."
These women have carried on, as I said before, absolutely without any charge on the government. I do not know much about what Toronto has done, but in Peterborough sixty-one typists gave 1,244 hours of service in connection with the mobilization of the Prince of Wales regiment. Our women volunteered to supervise the extra children that have been thrust upon the Children's Aid Society; they have atended classes in home nursing; they are driving cars; they go to the training centre in Peterborough three evenings a week; they do playground supervision work and welfare department work; they take part in the Red Cross and community fund drives, and many other activities. I should like to know from the minister just why he decided to do away with this association after it was formed, and why he did not tell the ladies at that time.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: The question put by the hon. member for Peterborough West cannot be answered in a few minutes.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I do not care how long the minister takes as long as he gives these ladies a clear and proper explanation of why this was done.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
I shall do my best. It is most unfortunate that this controversy has arisen. One of the functions of the Department of National War Services as set out in the governing act of the department is the coordination of voluntary assistance. It was

felt desirable to recognize in a special way the splendid work that the women of Canada are doing in their communities. Since the women of Canada are making an important contribution to the war effort in a field which only the women can fill effectively, it was thought desirable to promote the coordination of the voluntary assistance being given by these women in different parts of Canada.
We were faced with two alternative courses of action. One course that was suggested was that we should ask all the national organizations such as the Imperial Order of the Daughters of the Empire, the Canadian Red Cross Society, the National Council of Women, the Catholic women's organization and other representative women's organizations to send representatives to Ottawa to attend a national conference to discuss the advisability of establishing a national organization for the promotion of the coordination of women's voluntary services throughout Canada. After a discussion with leading women in different parts of the country that course was abandoned on the ground that the various national women's organizations across Canada were doing their work excellently in their own respective fields and that there was no need of an additional women's organization of a national nature.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Who made that decision?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I made it.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: What organizations did the minister consult?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: I discussed the matter with a great many women in Canada upon whose judgment I relied. I did not discuss it with the national organizations.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
With
individuals?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
With individual people whose judgment I valued. There was practically no dissenting opinion on the subject. The view that was suggested and the view that was ultimately adopted was that if we were going to promote the coordination of women's voluntary services in an effective manner, we would have to do so on a community basis in the communities where the women would actually do the work. Therefore, as the basis for the coordination of women's voluntary services in this country, we adopted the principle of community solidarity. We decided that whatever we would do in promoting the coordination of women's voluntary services would be on a community basis.

War Appropriation-War Services

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: Is it not on a community basis now?

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext:
I did not interrupt my hon. friend. I shall be glad to answer any questions if he will just allow me to continue.
We came to the view also that the leadership among women is actually in the community, that the effective work that women can do is the work that they can do in their own community, and that is the general view. So we adopted as the basis of our whole organization the basis of community solidarity. It was thought at one time that we would merely divide our division of voluntary services and create a subdivision of it for the promotion of women's voluntary services coordination, but the view prevailed that the activities of the women of Canada in the community field deserved special recognition, and we set up an independent division of my department known as the women's voluntary services division. The purposes of that division are set out in the order in council which created the division. They are as follows:
To promote the coordination of the voluntary efforts of the women of Canada and to encourage the organization of women's voluntary services on a community basis with a view to their best utilization for the needs of their community, the maintenance of national morale and the furtherance of the welfare of the nation.
That is the purpose of the women's voluntary services division.

As a matter of fact, the decision with regard to the name had really been taken long before the actual order in council went through. If the name is an appropriate name for the division which, after all, is concerned with the promotion of the coordination of women's activities across Canada, it is more important that the name should be allocated to that division than to an organization which at the present time is purely provincial.

attempted to make it national, did they not?

one? They were there first.

the legal aspect.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR GRANTING TO HIS MAJESTY AID FOR NATIONAL DEFENCE AND SECURITY
speechtext: It is not organized on a community basis at all. The community activity has to take into account, if it is really to be a community enterprise, all the important community organizations, and it must of necessity include the charitable and social welfare agencies because they are the core of the community activities; it is necessary so far as possible to bring those agencies together in the community. One objective was to promote the establishment of a central volunteer bureau where all the women in the community could register their willingness to engage in some kind of voluntary effort. That central volunteer bureau will become a pool or reservoir of voluntary aid, so that any organization in the community that wishes to do so can go to the central volunteer bureau and say that it needs additional assistance for this or that activity, which might be a social welfare or a social agency activity of one kind or another. It might be a war loan campaign or a salvage campaign. It might take one of twenty or thirty different forms; but there would be that reservoir of voluntary women of the community, effective not only for the purposes of the war, but also for the purposes of the postwar period. We felt that was much sounder than to establish another provincial or national organization.

organization which my hon. friend mentions is not using the organizations that are in the

Unemployment Insurance
community. It rejects a number of them and does not want to have anything to do with some of them.

the social welfare organizations are the heart of the community, and you cannot have a community organized on the basis of community solidarity if you exclude the persons who are interested and concerned in that part of the community which is in need of social aid.
